questions.question: What authority does the Duke give Angelo before withdrawing from public view?

options.text: Power to govern Vienna and enforce or temper its laws.
Power to advise Escalus while leaving all judgments to him.
Power to enforce the laws while granting no mercy himself.
Power to govern the prisons while the Duke stays in court.

questions.explanation: The Duke appoints Angelo to act fully in his place, with Escalus as his secondary.

evidence.exact:
DUKE.
Angelo,
There is a kind of character in thy life
That to th’ observer doth thy history
Fully unfold. Thyself and thy belongings
Are not thine own so proper as to waste
Thyself upon thy virtues, they on thee.
Heaven doth with us as we with torches do,
Not light them for themselves; for if our virtues
Did not go forth of us, ’twere all alike
As if we had them not. Spirits are not finely touched
But to fine issues; nor nature never lends
The smallest scruple of her excellence
But, like a thrifty goddess, she determines
Herself the glory of a creditor,
Both thanks and use. But I do bend my speech
To one that can my part in him advertise.
Hold, therefore, Angelo.
In our remove be thou at full ourself.
Mortality and mercy in Vienna
Live in thy tongue and heart. Old Escalus,
Though first in question, is thy secondary.
Take thy commission.

evidence.exact:
DUKE.
My haste may not admit it;
Nor need you, on mine honour, have to do
With any scruple. Your scope is as mine own,
So to enforce or qualify the laws
As to your soul seems good. Give me your hand;
I’ll privily away. I love the people,
But do not like to stage me to their eyes.
Though it do well, I do not relish well
Their loud applause and Aves vehement;
Nor do I think the man of safe discretion
That does affect it. Once more, fare you well.

questions.question: What has led to Claudio’s imprisonment?

options.text: His refusal to serve Angelo in the army.
His sexual relationship with Juliet before their marriage was publicly formalized.
His attempt to steal Mariana’s lost dowry.

questions.explanation: Claudio describes their contract and the missing outward ceremony; Juliet’s pregnancy has exposed their relationship.

evidence.exact:
CLAUDIO.
Thus stands it with me: upon a true contract
I got possession of Julietta’s bed.
You know the lady; she is fast my wife,
Save that we do the denunciation lack
Of outward order. This we came not to
Only for propagation of a dower
Remaining in the coffer of her friends,
From whom we thought it meet to hide our love
Till time had made them for us. But it chances
The stealth of our most mutual entertainment
With character too gross is writ on Juliet.

evidence.exact:
CLAUDIO.
Unhappily, even so.
And the new deputy now for the Duke—
Whether it be the fault and glimpse of newness,
Or whether that the body public be
A horse whereon the governor doth ride,
Who, newly in the seat, that it may know
He can command, lets it straight feel the spur;
Whether the tyranny be in his place,
Or in his eminence that fills it up,
I stagger in—but this new governor
Awakes me all the enrolled penalties
Which have, like unscoured armour, hung by th’ wall
So long that nineteen zodiacs have gone round,
And none of them been worn; and for a name
Now puts the drowsy and neglected act
Freshly on me. ’Tis surely for a name.

questions.question: What does Isabella ask Angelo to consider when she first pleads for Claudio?

options.text: Whether Claudio could pay a larger fine than Pompey.
Whether Juliet could enter a convent instead.
Whether he shares the human weakness for which he condemns her brother.
Whether Escalus should replace the Duke permanently.

questions.explanation: She urges Angelo to search his own heart before condemning her brother’s life.

evidence.exact:
ISABELLA.
Because authority, though it err like others,
Hath yet a kind of medicine in itself
That skins the vice o’ th’ top. Go to your bosom,
Knock there, and ask your heart what it doth know
That’s like my brother’s fault. If it confess
A natural guiltiness such as is his,
Let it not sound a thought upon your tongue
Against my brother’s life.

questions.question: What does Angelo demand from Isabella in exchange for Claudio’s life?

options.text: That she marry Lucio immediately.
That she pay Mariana’s missing dowry.
That she reveal where the Duke is hiding.
That she submit sexually to him.

questions.explanation: Angelo explicitly makes her yielding her body the price of redeeming her brother.

evidence.exact:
ANGELO.
Who will believe thee, Isabel?
My unsoiled name, th’ austereness of my life,
My vouch against you, and my place i’ th’ state
Will so your accusation overweigh
That you shall stifle in your own report,
And smell of calumny. I have begun,
And now I give my sensual race the rein.
Fit thy consent to my sharp appetite;
Lay by all nicety and prolixious blushes
That banish what they sue for. Redeem thy brother
By yielding up thy body to my will;
Or else he must not only die the death,
But thy unkindness shall his death draw out
To ling’ring sufferance. Answer me tomorrow,
Or, by the affection that now guides me most,
I’ll prove a tyrant to him. As for you,
Say what you can, my false o’erweighs your true.

questions.question: How does Claudio react when fear of death overcomes him?

options.text: He begs Isabella to save him even through the sin she condemns.
He urges Isabella to expose Angelo and accept his execution.
He asks the Provost to execute Juliet in his place.
He refuses to speak again unless the Duke returns.

questions.explanation: Claudio imagines death’s terrors and asks his sister to let him live despite the moral cost.

evidence.exact:
CLAUDIO.
Ay, but to die, and go we know not where;
To lie in cold obstruction, and to rot;
This sensible warm motion to become
A kneaded clod; and the delighted spirit
To bathe in fiery floods, or to reside
In thrilling regions of thick-ribbed ice;
To be imprisoned in the viewless winds
And blown with restless violence round about
The pendent world; or to be worse than worst
Of those that lawless and incertain thought
Imagine howling—’tis too horrible.
The weariest and most loathed worldly life
That age, ache, penury, and imprisonment
Can lay on nature is a paradise
To what we fear of death.

questions.question: What substitution does the disguised Duke arrange for Isabella’s meeting with Angelo?

options.text: Juliet will go in Mariana’s place.
Mariana will go in Isabella’s place.
Isabella will go in Juliet’s place.
Francisca will go in Mariana’s place.

questions.explanation: The Duke plans for Angelo’s abandoned betrothed Mariana to keep the appointment instead.

evidence.exact:
DUKE.
This forenamed maid hath yet in her the continuance of her first affection. His unjust unkindness, that in all reason should have quenched her love, hath, like an impediment in the current, made it more violent and unruly. Go you to Angelo; answer his requiring with a plausible obedience; agree with his demands to the point. Only refer yourself to this advantage: first, that your stay with him may not be long; that the time may have all shadow and silence in it; and the place answer to convenience. This being granted in course, and now follows all. We shall advise this wronged maid to stead up your appointment, go in your place. If the encounter acknowledge itself hereafter, it may compel him to her recompense; and here, by this, is your brother saved, your honour untainted, the poor Mariana advantaged, and the corrupt deputy scaled. The maid will I frame and make fit for his attempt. If you think well to carry this as you may, the doubleness of the benefit defends the deceit from reproof. What think you of it?

Send Claudio’s head despite the Duke’s plan.
Use Ragozine’s head after his death from fever.

evidence.exact:
PROVOST.
Here in the prison, father,
There died this morning of a cruel fever
One Ragozine, a most notorious pirate,
A man of Claudio’s years; his beard and head
Just of his colour. What if we do omit
This reprobate till he were well inclined,
And satisfy the Deputy with the visage
Of Ragozine, more like to Claudio?

questions.question: What does Isabella ask for Angelo while she still believes Claudio dead?

options.text: Mercy and the sparing of Angelo’s life.
Execution without allowing Mariana to plead.
Marriage to Angelo in exchange for his pardon.
Exile for Mariana as Angelo’s accomplice.

questions.explanation: At Mariana’s urging, Isabella kneels and asks that Angelo not die.

evidence.exact:
ISABELLA.
[Kneeling.] Most bounteous sir,
Look, if it please you, on this man condemned
As if my brother lived. I partly think
A due sincerity governed his deeds
Till he did look on me. Since it is so,
Let him not die. My brother had but justice,
In that he did the thing for which he died.
For Angelo,
His act did not o’ertake his bad intent,
And must be buried but as an intent
That perished by the way. Thoughts are no subjects;
Intents but merely thoughts.

Lucio reveals that Ragozine was Isabella’s brother.

questions.explanation: Claudio is unmuffled alive, and the Duke pardons him before extending remission to Angelo.
